title: Improving Topic Modeling by Distilling Soft Labels from Language Models
subcategory: distilling language-model soft labels into neural topic models
task: Training neural topic models with contextual reconstruction targets
problem: NTMs reconstruct sparse bag-of-words vectors, ignoring context and suffering from data sparsity; prompting-based LLM topic models are costly and do not give probabilistic topic distributions.
architecture: DSL: a small language model is prompted to produce a one-word theme label for each document; its next-token probabilities are projected onto the topic vocabulary (temperature-scaled) to form a soft target; the topic model (ProdLDA, ECRTM or FASTopic backbone) takes the LM's last hidden state as input and is trained with a KL loss to reconstruct the soft target.
llm_or_encoder: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama3.2-1B-Instruct, Phi-3-mini, Qwen-3.5-0.8B, ERNIE-4.5-0.3B; GTE-large-en-v1.5 for embedding baselines
key_results: Every backbone-LM combination with DSL significantly outperforms all baselines on Purity; FASTopic + DSL keeps I-RBO = 1.000 on all three datasets.
ProdLDA + DSL with ERNIE-4.5-0.3B: C_V .381, Purity .520 on 20NewsGroup and Purity .737 on StackOverflow; replacing soft targets by BoW drops StackOverflow Purity by .363.
strengths: Works with sub-1B language models, so it is cheaper than prompting-based LLM topic modelling.
Keeps explicit, interpretable document-topic and topic-word distributions.
Introduces a retrieval-based evaluation of document-topic distributions.

limitations.text: Using the KL loss trades some C_V for higher diversity and Purity compared with NLL.
Vocabulary restricted to words that are single tokens under the LM tokenizer.
Only English datasets; prompting strategies beyond a single instruction left for future work.

notes: Averaged over K = 25, 50, 75, 100 with five seeds.
